items.title: Peterson: Here’s what Bessent’s about-face on Jensen Huang reveals about Trump and China
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was becoming the face of an emerging harder line on Nvidia— until he reversed course
items.body: For a minute there, it seemed like someone in the Trump administration might actually be willing to stand up to China. For about a week and a half, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was the face of an emerging harder line on Nvidia over the potential risks its co-founder Jensen Huang 's affairs posed to national security. Bessent was giving voice to China hawks who had felt sidelined by the Trump administration's willingness to sell artificial intelligence chips to China. They see China's AI program as a major threat, and want to restrain its growth by cutting off the supply of advanced chips to China. The resignation of Huang, who pressed the Trump Administration to allow the exports, seemed to signal that the hawks had found new influence in Washington. By this weekend, Bessent had softened his public resistance to Huang's reinstatement.

items.title: Nvidia surge: What investors should do with the stock and the AI trade now
items.summary: The market is loving the return of Jensen Huang, but investors and lawmakers have their guards up.
items.body: Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated. Investors and traders said that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January. "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday? Of course not, you can't be," said Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, which counted Nvidia as its largest position as he bought on the dip over the last few weeks.

items.summary: Huang's role at the centre of his company's journey to lynchpin of AI proved crucial.
items.body: There have been three jaw-dropping moments in the past few hours around Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia chief executive after he admitted an affair with a woman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy. The shock announcement of his return to the chipmaker was followed by the addition of one trillion dollars of stock market value to Nvidia. Then it was the moment President Trump admitted the obvious: that it was his "You're unfired" message direct to the board that changed the decision. The nature of the U-turn is clear from what Nvidia was saying just last week. The board was clear that Huang was not returning. The interim management had also suggested some shifts in strategy away from the Huang era. This is a comeback that exceeds the return of Sam Altman to OpenAI or Steve Jobs to Apple, in terms of sheer numbers.

items.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervenes
items.summary: Share price surges as chipmaker reverses decision to remove chief executive after US president ‘convinced’ its board Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment US politics – live updates Timeline: fall and comeback of Jensen Huang Nvidia has reinstated…
items.body: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after Donald Trump directly intervened with the US AI chipmaker’s board of directors, in a stunning reversal of the tech billionaire’s downfall . Speaking on Monday shortly after Nvidia’s surprise announcement that Huang had been restored to the top job – less than two weeks after he resigned – Trump said that he had “convinced” the board to do it. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC. Huang had resigned after reports of extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees. “It’s very exciting news. I felt very strongly that he should come back,” the US president said. Huang said he was “honored to return to Nvidia” and lead “one of the most consequential technology companies in the world”.

items.title: Nvidia reinstates former CEO Jensen Huang despite China espionage scandal
items.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring back the disgraced CEO, who resigned this month amid news of his affairs. He's suspected of having had a relationship with a Chinese intelligence asset.
items.body: US tech company Nvidia said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO "effective immediately." This follows just a matter of days after his resignation after admitting to extramarital affairs, reportedly including a dalliance with a woman who was a Chinese intelligence asset. The board unanimously decided that his return was in the "best interests of the company," Nvidia said, adding that it was satisfied that Huang had demonstrated his "candor and ability to lead." Meanwhile, the 63-year-old said in a statement that he was "honored" to return to the company and that he would take on the renewed responsibility "with the greatest humility and renewed commitment." He thanked interim CEO Colette Kress , who is set to return to her role as chief financial officer.

items.title: The biggest money-making energy trade looks over. What to buy instead
items.summary: The epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding.
items.body: Is one of the greatest money-making trades of the last few years coming to an end? No, I'm not talking about Nvidia or any of the data center- or AI-related power companies (although they have been crushed lately too… more on that on CNBC TV. Tune in!). I'm talking about whether the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding. Over the last year, the jump in some of these companies has been nothing short of remarkable. That jump is largely due to massive increases in margins, earnings, and cash flow. Those have occurred because of a big jump in what is called a crack spread . That is the difference between the price of oil and the finished price of refined products such as diesel and jet fuel. For most of this year, spreads have been soaring as disruptions and attacks on facilities and shipping in the Arabian Gulf, Hormuz, and deep inside Russia have played havoc with the market.

items.title: Nvidia value climbs by almost $1tn and tech stocks rally after Jensen Huang returns
items.summary: The jump in Nvidia shares has also lifted stock markets, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq up 6.5%.
items.body: Nvidia's market value rose by nearly $1 trillion as its share price skyrocketed after the tech firm reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive with immediate effect. His shock reinstatement comes less than two weeks after Huang resigned after admitting an affair with a woman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy, a period in which shares in the chipmaker have also fallen significantly. Nvidia shares rose by more than 31% which also lifted stock markets, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq climbing by 6.5% and the S&P 500 also rose 4.75%. Tech stocks more broadly have also rallied following large falls on Friday , with much of the rally starting in pre-market trading before Huang's return was announced. Other chipmakers experienced large increases following Monday's announcement from the Nvidia board. Shares in Micron Technology jumped 19%, while AMD shares rose nearly 7%.

items.title: Next issues cyber-attack warning after ‘benign’ data accessed by hackers
items.summary: Retailer says it believes no personal data that could lead to fraud was accessed after hack of third-party supplier Next has warned that hackers have gained access to data relating to the clothing and homewares retailer through a technology supplier. The company, which has more…
items.body: Next has warned that hackers have gained access to data relating to the clothing and homewares retailer through a technology supplier. The company, which has more than 800 stores in the UK and Ireland and sells via 200 stores overseas, said on Monday that it had been informed that one of its third-party suppliers had “experienced a cyber incident” resulting in unauthorised access to the data. The high street chain said it believed that customers’ personal data had not been compromised and the information affected was “limited in nature and, based on our current assessment, cannot be used to facilitate fraud against our customers or Next”. It is understood the data accessed does not include information such as contact details, addresses, passwords or bank details, which could be used to commit fraud.

items.title: 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
items.summary: For decades, Germans have known Hollywood's biggest stars through the same familiar voices. Now an AI clause in Netflix contracts is splitting the industry over whether it protects performers or exposes them.
items.body: When does Cameron Diaz not sound like Cameron Diaz? When you're in a German cinema. For more than 30 years, whenever the Oscar -winning actor has appeared on German screens, she has spoken with the voice of Katrin Fröhlich. The same goes for all other famous actors. In Germany's €125-million ($138-million) voiceover industry, Hollywood 's up-and-comers are "adopted" by a voice actor who provides their German voice — often for decades — ensuring continuity and a certain relationship to the stars for audiences. But on Netflix, and perhaps elsewhere, many of those voices might be about to change. Recently, Fröhlich and fellow voice actors Anne Helm (Margot Robbie) and Luise Helm (Scarlett Johansson) published a video on social media, letting their followers know they wouldn't provide their voices anymore.

items.title: Trump tells CNBC ‘I made the deal’ to reinstate Nvidia’s Jensen Huang
items.summary: President Trump said his administration gave Nvidia's board assurance that Jensen Huang would not be a national security threat if he was reinstated as CEO.
items.body: President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday morning that he spoke directly to Nvidia 's board and urged them to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang . "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview shortly after Nvidia's shock announcement that Huang was returning to lead the tech giant. Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang came less than two weeks after he resigned. Huang had stepped down after admitting he cheated on his wife and amid claims his affairs included one with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees. Huang's relationship with the suspected spy, Alice Huang, and her role as an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed raised concerns that she was facilitating the diversion of Nvidia's most advanced semiconductor chip to China. Trump said Nvidia's board "did ask for assurance on the national security threat," Trump said.

items.title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?
items.summary: The Nvidia chief executive has been at the centre of the artificial intelligence boom.
items.body: Nvidia and its co-founder Jensen Huang have been at the centre of the artificial intelligence (AI) spending boom. No company or chief executive has arguably been more consequential to the development of AI in recent years, with the US microchip manufacturer under Huang positioning itself as a critical cog in the development of the world-changing technology. That central position prompted questions, in the aftermath of Huang's departure over revelations of extramarital affairs, over how important he was to the wider AI industry and US economy. The fact he has been handed his job back after just 11 days in a U-turn by Nvidia's board implies the top brass believe Huang is irreplaceable. Shares in the company have surged on the news of Huang's shock return, following a period of sharp declines.

items.summary: Shares are volatile amid jitters over tech and AI – but think carefully before you decide to ditch investments too It has been a volatile time on global stock markets, with rapid rallies and punishing sell-offs. There have been signs in recent weeks that investors are getting…
items.body: It has been a volatile time on global stock markets, with rapid rallies and punishing sell-offs. There have been signs in recent weeks that investors are getting cold feet over the outlook for AI companies and selling off technology stocks. Last week, the AI company Anthropic launched on to the market and had a record-breaking first day , but on Friday stock markets around the world tumbled and the US Nasdaq closed 5% below its mark on 1 January . On Monday, the dramatic return of Jensen Huang as chief executive of Nvidia sent its shares soaring and contributed to a jump in US stock markets. Investors seem to be losing faith in AI – or rather in the valuations of companies that are involved in the industry.

items.title: Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?
items.summary: Germany plans to pay €10 a month into investment accounts for children to encourage long-term retirement saving. Economists say the measure may help build wealth but won't solve the country's pension funding challenge.
items.body: Germany's pension system is under growing strain as demographic change leaves a shrinking workforce funding the pensions of an increasing number of retirees. In the 1960s, for instance, six workers contributed to the pay-as-you-go public retirement system for each pensioner. Today, that figure has fallen to just two contributors per retiree. According to the Federal Statistical Office, Germany's fertility rate is currently 1.32 children per woman, and has remained below the 2.1 needed to maintain a stable population since the 1970s. As a large cohort of baby boomers reaches retirement age, fewer young people are entering the workforce. Germany's working-age population is shrinking by around 1% each year due to demographic change alone, according to the German bank LBBW.

items.summary: Wall Street strategists say Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia could steady the AI trade, though spending and data-center risks remain.
items.body: The major averages of U.S. equities surged on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, giving investors some hope that the relentless selling pressure seen last week may subside — at least temporarily. The relief rally came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average , S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended Friday's session in correction territory . The S&P alone tumbled more than 9% after Huang's departure from the chipmaker was initially announced on Nov. 12 through Friday. That sell-off may be over — at least temporarily — according to Wall Street experts. But key questions linger around Nvidia and the artificial intelligence trade that has carried the bull market. "I think the AI trade is back on," said Mark Gibbens, founder of Gibbens Capital Management.

items.title: The rise and fall and rise again of Jensen Huang
items.summary: Days after resigning while mired in scandal of extra-marital affairs, Nvidia's Jensen Huang is making a remarkable return.
items.body: For a long time it seemed that Jensen Huang, the leather jacket-clad founder of Nvidia, dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech", could do no wrong. Then came allegations of two affairs - one with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy - that rocked the world of tech and the global stock market. Huang resigned. Now, just 11 days later, he's been reinstated by the board, who says it believes he is the right person to lead the company. So what do we know about the man who is once again at the head of Nvidia, a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China? Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg. But his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential.

items.title: Flagship UK gigafactory plan in turmoil after it loses second builder in five months
items.summary: Tata-owned Agratas plant to build EV batteries for sister company Jaguar Land Rover seen as crucial for long-term health of British car industry One of the UK’s flagship electric vehicle battery projects has been thrown into turmoil after its second building contractor in five…
items.body: One of the UK’s flagship electric vehicle battery projects has been thrown into turmoil after its second building contractor in five months walked away, adding to questions over when Jaguar Land Rover cars will use British-made batteries. The £5.2bn gigafactory in Bridgwater, Somerset, is being built by Agratas, to provide batteries for Britain’s largest automotive employer, its sister company. Agratas and Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) are both part of Indian conglomerate Tata Group. The UK government has pledged £380m in financial support for the factory because it is seen as crucial to the long-term survival of the British car industry, but the build has suffered several setbacks. The construction specialist contracted by Agratas, TSL, has decided to leave the project after failing to agree terms with the battery company, according to three sources.

items.title: San Francisco is enjoying an AI boom, but worries about a crash are growing
items.summary: AI employees in the industry's epicentre - San Francisco - worry that the sector is overheated.
items.body: Lauren Goldboss is busy. The owner of a small San Francisco dog-walking company, she has been hiring staff and buying vans. Fuelling the growth is her new office dog-walking service Paw Perk, popular with some local AI start-ups. Her business is an example of how the AI boom in San Francisco is benefiting other sectors. The city saw an exodus of residents during the pandemic and its downtown was weakened by remote work, but it's now enjoying a rejuvenation, with AI being the major driver. Leading AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic – which have been hiring top engineering talent, often on eye-popping salaries – are based here. Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, last week listed on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange. Signs of the boom are evident in soaring rents and house prices, falling office vacancies, and buses and billboards plastered with cryptic AI adverts.

items.summary: Price plunges 70% as Adolfo Hernandez leaves with ‘immediate effect’ amid continued fallout from pension payment problems The chief executive of the troubled outsourcing group Capita has abruptly departed as he admitted it has “not delivered” for retired civil servants left…
items.body: The chief executive of the troubled outsourcing group Capita has abruptly departed as he admitted it has “not delivered” for retired civil servants left waiting for pension payments. Adolfo Hernandez has agreed to step down with “immediate effect”, the company said on Monday. He is to be replaced by the chief financial officer, Pablo Andres. Shares in Capita plunged by 70% to as low as 72p, Capita’s lowest share price since October 1991, on Monday as it cut profit forecasts and proposed raising £190m in extra capital. Capita said that adjusted operating profit in 2027 was expected to be £85m to £95m lower than previously expected, due to extra costs in relation to the UK Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS) contract, and “short-term contract headwinds”.

items.body: Gianni Infantino’s failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan could have locked football in for up to 96 years while paying its management up to 5% of the scheme’s multibillion-pound value, according to documents seen by the Guardian. Previously undisclosed communications by Fifa and Thrive Capital, the lead investor for the proposal, cast fresh light on the deal to sell off football’s crown jewels. They outline a plan, produced days before July’s final of the 2026 World Cup , to profit from the sport’s burgeoning commercial revenues for almost a century. Infantino hopes to be re-elected for a fourth term as president in March and is the favourite to win that contest . In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications. If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

items.title: SpaceX sued by Oregon and Virginia over AI deepfake porn, Grok safety claims
items.summary: The states are seeking civil penalties and injunctions to stop Grok and X from creation and distribution of nonconsensual sexualized images.
items.body: Lawsuits against Elon Musk's SpaceX are stacking up, with Virginia and Oregon becoming the first states to sue the company over issues with its Grok AI image generator. Versions of Grok and SpaceX's social network X have enabled users to generate and distribute explicit deepfakes based on real photos or videos of children and other people who did not consent, according to research by the Internet Watch Foundation , the Center for Countering Digital Hate and others. In separate complaints submitted to state courts as of Monday morning, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones argued that SpaceX failed to put safeguards in place to stop Grok and X users from making and sharing harmful deepfake images, especially alleged AI-generated child sexual abuse material.

items.body: Next has said that some of its data has been accessed in a cyber breach affecting a third-party online supplier. The high street retailer said there was no evidence that customers' personal data had been compromised. The firm - which has its headquarters in Enderby, Leicestershire - said it had been informed by one of its suppliers about the incident, which led to "unauthorised access to certain benign data relating to Next". "We took immediate steps to investigate the nature and scope of the incident with the supplier," the company told investors. "Our investigations are ongoing. However, current evidence indicates that no customer personal data has been compromised.

items.body: Compass, one of the biggest companies in the FTSE 100, is planning to switch its primary listing from London to the US in the latest blow to the struggling UK stock market. The £43.6bn ($57bn) catering firm, which has been listed in London since 1988, could announce its intention to move its listing to New York as soon as Tuesday when it reports its annual results. Compass is a big government contractor, providing meals in more than 2,000 schools, academies, colleges and universities across the UK and in some NHS hospitals, as well as offices in the private sector. Its franchise partners have included the likes of Starbucks, Costa and Taco Bell. Last year, the company made about three-quarters of its $3bn profit in North America.

items.body: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday hosted his third cryptocurrency gala for top holders of his meme coin, $TRUMP, which has plummeted to below $1 a coin after reaching a high of $75 the day before Trump's second inauguration, on Jan. 19, 2025. The dinner, held at the Trump National golf club in Sterling, Virginia, comes as some Democrats say they will investigate potential conflicts of interest and accuse Trump of using the presidency to boost his personal wealth. At Sunday's dinner, Trump maintained that his support for cryptocurrencies was to boost American economic competitiveness. "I'm doing it for the United States ... If we don't do it, China's going to do it," he told attendees, The Guardian reported. The event also featured speeches from boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, "Shark Tank" investor Kevin O'Leary and NBA champion Tristan Thompson.

items.summary: Jump in price follows slowdown in Qatar supplies and depleted summer stocks due to heatwaves European gas prices surged on Monday as a forecast cold snap in the coming weeks fed fears across the continent’s over depleted supply this winter and costly household bills. The Dutch…
items.body: European gas prices surged on Monday as a forecast cold snap in the coming weeks fed fears across the continent’s over depleted supply this winter and costly household bills. The Dutch month-ahead contract – the European benchmark for gas prices over the next four weeks – rose by as much as 8.6% to €96.08, before settling up 4% at €92.50. The jump in gas prices comes as much of north-west Europe braces for a tough winter, when energy demand is at its highest. Europe’s gas supplies have been hit by a slowdown in exports from Qatar due to the war in the Middle East, as well as an increase in consumption during the summer to power refrigeration and cooling during the prolonged heatwave. Storage levels on the continent are now well below the seasonal average, at about 69% full against a typical level of 80%.

items.title: Energy bills will soar - here's how you can ease the pain
items.summary: Household energy bills are about to increase but there are ways to keep a lid on your expenditure.
items.body: Energy prices are forecast to rise by 26% for millions of homes in January, but experts say there are ways to keep a check on rising bills. Energy regulator Ofgem's price cap, as well as suppliers' fixed deals, set a limit on the price of each unit of energy, not the total bill. So, you pay for what you use. Millions of people have cut back on their energy consumption during years of relatively high prices. With the unit price of gas, in particular, set to soar, experts say you should take a fresh look at your energy use and renew good habits. These are small changes but - alongside washing clothes at 30C, blocking draughts and batch cooking - they can reduce energy use and bills. Ofgem says about five million people still pay their bill when it arrives every three months, rather than receive a monthly bill often initially based on an estimate.

items.title: Cost of renting in Britain to rise twice as fast as buying amid shortage of properties
items.summary: Rents to rise by 14% until at least 2029, Hamptons predicts, as high demand for properties and low supply push up costs for tenants The cost of renting a home in Britain is expected to rise about twice as fast as that of buying one until at least 2029, according to research,…
items.body: The cost of renting a home in Britain is expected to rise about twice as fast as that of buying one until at least 2029, according to research, with shrinking supply pushing up the prices paid by tenants. Rents on newly agreed lets are forecast to grow by 14.2% between 2026 and 2029, compared with house price growth of 7.2%, according to forecasts from estate agent Hamptons. It said it expected growth in rents to peak at 4.5% in 2027 across Great Britain, before growing by an estimated 3.5% in 2028 and 2.5% in 2029. The supply of homes available to rent is expected to remain under pressure as landlords face higher costs and tighter regulation. Rents are usually set by the balance between supply and demand, and fewer rental homes will keep upward pressure on what landlords charge.

items.title: Netflix’s ‘The Altruists’ sparks FTX portrayal debate among crypto bigwigs from CZ to Star Xu
items.summary: Netflix’s "The Altruists" has drawn backlash over its portrayal of the FTX collapse, with prominent crypto industry figures questioning the series’ accuracy
items.body: Netflix's "The Altruists," released Nov. 19, has sparked backlash from prominent cryptocurrency industry figures, including Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, over its portrayal of the collapse of FTX. Critics have questioned the accuracy of the series' portrayal of the FTX collapse, particularly how it assigns responsibility of the scandal. Several crypto industry figures argue that it softens the culpability of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison while casting Zhao — widely known as CZ — as an outsized villain. Zhao criticized the series in a post on X , calling it "insane" and questioning whether the show was intended to influence public perception. He declined to comment to CNBC beyond his social-media posts. Zhao pleaded guilty in 2023 to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program at Binance, in violation of the U.S.

items.title: Poundland is facing collapse - what's gone wrong?
items.summary: Poundland has a matter of days to find a buyer or face collapsing into administration. Why?
items.body: The future of Poundland hangs in the balance as it faces a possible collapse into administration. Its owner, US investment firm Gordon Brothers, put it up for sale in September, but then rejected offers to keep the business afloat. Poundland has a major presence on the High Street, with 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, where it trades under the Dealz brand. If it were to collapse, the jobs of its 11,000 employees would be at risk, as well as potentially thousands of others at firms that supply the retailer. Although the chain was struggling when it was sold by Pepco last year for £1, the business turned a corner over the year to September, going from a £68m loss to an £18.1m profit before interest, tax and certain accounting charges. Going into the vital Christmas period, first-quarter like-for-like sales were up 7% and operational profits of £1.9m were up £1.2m on last year.

items.title: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment | Nils Pratley
items.summary: Jensen Huang’s return as CEO comes despite fact board hasn’t completed investigation into reports of affair with alleged Chinese spy Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO What was it that Nvidia’s board was saying about there being no chance of Jensen Huang coming back? The…
items.body: What was it that Nvidia’s board was saying about there being no chance of Jensen Huang coming back? The position – a mere six days ago – was supposed to be definitive. The exit of the co-founder came after “disclosure of personal behaviour inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards and cultural norms”, said Harvey Jones, who had been rapidly installed as chair of the chipmaker. The board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” after he “voluntarily resigned”, added Jones . The contribution of the US treasury secretary was equally forceful. Scott Bessent was already focused on the need for a new-broom external hire to replace Huang amid the scrutiny over Nvidia’s compliance with US export controls. “They need to go outside the company,” he said, calling for “a dramatic shake-up”. Those statements are now inoperative, in the famous phrase of Ron Ziegler .

items.title: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in $44 billion deal as AI supercharges cyberattacks
items.summary: CrowdStrike and competitors have shelled out billions to ramp up defenses in the wake of AI cyberattacks.
items.body: CrowdStrike plans to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal that combines two significant security businesses at a time when artificial intelligence is supercharging attacks. The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028. Under the agreement, Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share. CrowdStrike's acquisition pushes the Austin, Texas-based cyber vendor into the network security market and comes amid a massive year for cybersecurity deal-making in the wake of high-profile hacks like Hugging Face. "With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in a statement.

Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say
items.summary: Disability Minister Sir Stephen Timms says he will recommend major reforms to the personal independence payment.
items.body: A review into the personal independence payment (Pip) will call for a "fundamental overhaul" of the assessment process to "better recognise people's varying costs and needs", the disability minister has said. Sir Stephen Timms has been looking into disability benefits in England and Wales for the past year and found the set up was "no longer fit for purpose". Writing in the Times , external , he said his review, to be published on Tuesday, would recommend people with the most severe conditions have a "fast track" process which is "less burdensome". It comes after a separate review into young people not in education, employment or training (Neets) recommended Pip be scrapped and replaced for under-25s.

items.title: Anthropic’s IPO was great for the tech elite – and not so great for the rest of us | Steven Greenhouse
items.summary: The company’s co-founders are now wildly rich, while countless Americans face AI-driven threats to their jobs and fears of a stock bubble The sultans of Silicon Valley and the wizards of Wall Street rejoiced this week when Anthropic raised an eye-popping $81bn in the largest…
items.body: T he sultans of Silicon Valley and the wizards of Wall Street rejoiced this week when Anthropic raised an eye-popping $81bn in the largest initial public offering in history. They saw the AI company’s IPO as a gung-ho affirmation of Silicon Valley’s and Wall Street’s marriage of technology and capitalism. For many employees at the company that developed Claude, the public offering must have been a thing of dreams. With the IPO valuing Anthropic at $1.5tn, the company’s seven co-founders each came away with stakes worth about $20bn , while, by one estimate , 600 of Anthropic’s more than 5,000 employees will have holdings topping $100m and 2,800 others will have shares worth more than $10m.

items.title: 26-year-old Google worker earns $323,000 a year—but lives on less than minimum wage
items.summary: Charles Broomfield set a post-college goal of reaching $750,000 in investments by age 30. Now 26, he expects to get there within the next year.
items.body: This story is part of CNBC Make It's Millennial Money series, which details how people around the world earn, spend and save their money. At 26 years old, Google AI security analyst and YouTuber Charles Broomfield is on track to earn about $323,000 this year — but he lives on less than minimum wage. For the past few years, Broomfield has kept his annual spending on core living expenses under $20,000, less than the roughly $23,700 a full-time worker would earn at the minimum wage, averaged across all 50 states. He does it by living with roommates in Washington, D.C., walking or biking instead of driving, eating free meals at work and rarely spending beyond his basic needs. Even when he splurges on something fun, he keeps things modest; in August, that meant a baseball game and a single $7 beer.

items.title: South East Water reports loss after supply issues
items.summary: South East Water records a pre-tax loss of £22.9m in the six months to 30 September.
items.body: South East Water has reported a half-year loss after penalties and £29m of costs following disruption to water supplies over the summer. The company, which serves about 2.4 million customers across south-east England, recorded a pre-tax loss of £22.9m in the six months to 30 September, compared with a profit of £18.2m during the same period last year. In July, regulator Ofwat ordered the company to spend £30.5m on improvements after supply interruptions hit customers across Kent and Sussex which affected more than 286,000 customers. The company spent £29m responding to further supply interruptions during summer heatwaves in Kent and Sussex . This included providing bottled water, setting up emergency water stations and compensating customers. South East Water said it had set aside £14.6m in its latest financial results to cover the redress package.

items.title: Apple iPhone Duo review: the most novel and interesting iPhone in almost a decade
items.summary: The folding iPhone is early-adopter gold, changing the way iOS works and successfully condensing a tablet into your pocket, but it is not for everyone Apple’s first folding phone has upended the usual order of things with some interesting choices about how you use a iPhone – for…
items.body: Apple’s first folding phone has upended the usual order of things with some interesting choices about how you use a iPhone – for better or worse. The Duo sits atop the pile as Apple’s most expensive smartphone – at £1,999 (€2,299/$1,999/A$3,499) it costs more than most of its folding Android rivals and as much as the iPhone 18 Pro Max and the latest iPad mini combined. It is designed as a pocketable device that replaces your phone and tablet but it is neither a regular iPhone when closed nor an iPad when open, it’s something else entirely. The Duo is a squat, wide and weighty device, flying in the face of eight years of folding Androids that have generally been tall and thin . The outside 5.4in screen is bright, crisp and smooth. Open the Duo like a book to reveal its fantastic 7.6in folding OLED screen with a matt finish similar to the company’s high-end iPads , MacBooks and displays .

items.title: U.S. probes Megaspeed, Alice Huang as new figure emerges in Nvidia chip case
items.summary: The U.S. is investigating Megaspeed and Alice Huang after it emerged a former associate of hers was reportedly "deeply involved" in the firm's activities
items.body: The U.S. is investigating Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said, as a report identified one of her associates as a key decision-maker at the Singapore-based company. Clayton said the investigation was "ongoing" on Sunday, the day before Nvidia announced it had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a position he resigned from in part because of his relationship with Alice Huang. Alice Huang was a key figure in Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia. U.S. intelligence reportedly believes she is a Chinese spy. "There is an investigation ongoing into her firm and into her," Clayton told ABC on Sunday, adding that, "Nvidia chips, they are the jewel.

items.title: ‘It’s an embarrassment’: how LA’s desperately needed airport tram went off the rails
items.summary: The SkyLink people mover is less than 2.5 miles long but it’s $1bn over budget and has been delayed by four years What purportedly modern, world-class city has an airport where millions of visitors step off their planes, glide their bags on to the sidewalk and are greeted by a…
items.body: W hat purportedly modern, world-class city has an airport where millions of visitors step off their planes, glide their bags on to the sidewalk and are greeted by a terrifying scrum of bumper-to-bumper traffic? A journey to the Los Angeles international airport (LAX) is notorious for its dreaded gridlock, the result of an outdated horseshoe street design that offers only one way in and out of one of the busiest airports in the world. “You have to really love somebody to drive them to LAX,” said Eli Lipmen, executive director of Move LA , a local non-profit coalition that organizes for improved transit and housing. Enter the people mover: a long-awaited rail line of less than 2.5 miles (4km) that would offer congestion relief by finally providing a direct rail connection between terminals, a ride-share zone, a new transit center and a car rental hub.

items.title: Tokenized stocks face pushback as NYSE, Nasdaq pivot for a new market
items.summary: OKXICE is set to debut Monday despite objections from 90% of the companies whose stocks it initially proposed to list.
items.body: OKXICE, a trading platform for tokenized securities jointly operated by Intercontinental Exchange and crypto exchange OKX, is set to debut Monday despite objections from 90% of the companies whose stocks it initially proposed to list. Of the 62 companies whose shares OKXICE first sought to trade, 56 objected to having their shares tokenized and traded on the platform, according to a review of public notices posted between Oct. 4 and Nov. 5 . By last week, even more companies had objected , including those not on the original roster. The high objection rate may reflect companies' lack of readiness to have blockchain-based representations of their shares traded on a new third-party platform like OKXICE, rather than broad resistance to tokenization.

items.title: Welfare cuts: What's been happening with Pip and universal credit?
items.summary: The government commissioned a review into Pip last year after it was forced to water down planned cuts to benefits.
items.body: The assessment process of a key disability benefit should be overhauled to "better recognise people's varying costs and needs", the disability minister has said. Sir Stephen Timms has been leading a review into Personal Independence Payments (Pip) and has called the current system "not fit for purpose". The review was commissioned by the government last year after it was forced to water down planned cuts to benefits in the face of fierce opposition from backbench Labour MPs. Pip is paid to 3.7 million people with a long-term physical or mental health condition , external in England and Wales. It is not linked to someone's savings or income and does not affect other benefits, or the benefit cap , external . People can get Pip if they are working. Pip includes a daily living component and a mobility component. Claimants may be eligible for one or both.

items.title: Zelenskyy praises ‘exemplary’ drone operation that sank Russian warship in a Libyan port
items.summary: The incident comes alongside a suspected Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea over the weekend.
items.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday lauded an "exemplary" military operation that sank one of Russia's newest ships at a Libyan port, after Kyiv's forces struck their target with several domestically made naval drones. The incident followed a suspected Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and occurred less than a week after damage was inflicted on Russian President Vladimir Putin 's prized Crimea bridge. In a social media post , Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces deployed seven sea drones to attack the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, at Benghazi's port in the early hours of Sunday morning. Ukraine's president posted dramatic video footage showing Ukraine's naval drones triggering a massive explosion on the Russian ship. "Despite all the enemy's efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk.

items.title: Flights cancelled in Belgium due to cost-of-living strike
items.summary: A series of strikes have hit Belgium in recent months as the prime minister struggles to agree a budget to cut costs.
items.body: Hundreds of flights have been cancelled and public transport severely disrupted across Belgium as a result of a strike against planned austerity measures. All air traffic has been halted at Brussels Airport in Zaventem as well as at Charleroi, home to low-cost airlines such as Ryanair. Underground services have also been halted in capital Brussels, where large numbers of people joined a protest march. The protest comes as Prime Minister Bart De Wever continues talks with his coalition allies over a budget to cut borrowing costs. King Philippe declined his resignation earlier this month, giving De Wever more time to negotiate. No flights are taking off or landing at Brussels Airport between 07:00 and 21:00 local time (06:00-20:00 GMT) as a result of the strike by air traffic controllers.

items.title: Drivers trapped in limbo due to DVLA licence delays
items.summary: It had been revoked on medical grounds but after 12 months I was invited to restore it. Nine months later my application was untouched My driving licence was revoked on medical grounds after I underwent brain surgery for a vascular lesion in 2024. After waiting the required 12…
items.body: My driving licence was revoked on medical grounds after I underwent brain surgery for a vascular lesion in 2024. After waiting the required 12 months for my health to stabilise, I was invited to apply for my licence to be restored. I duly sent the evidence from hospital consultants and medical tests. That was nine months ago. Since then, the DVLA has left my application untouched. I phone it every month to be told my case has not been looked at yet and that no timeline for commencement of the review can be provided. I have written to my MP for help . I submitted a formal complaint via the DVLA website 31 days ago and received no response, despite its own acknowledgment that it “aims to respond fully within 10 working days ”. People who have undergone serious medical trauma are being treated as second -class citizens.

items.title: 2-year Treasury yield jumps as stocks rebound, investors await New York Fed President Williams speech
items.summary: U.S. Treasury yields rose Monday, partially unwinding price action seen at the end of last week, as stocks experienced a strong rebound on Wall Street.
items.body: Treasury yields on the short end of the curve rose on Monday, partially unwinding price action seen at the end of last week, as stocks experienced a strong rebound on Wall Street and investors looked ahead to comments from John Williams of the New York Fed. The 2-year Treasury note yield , the most sensitive to short-term Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, was up more than 7 basis points at 4.69%. The 10-year Treasury yield — the key benchmark for mortgages, student loans and credit card debt — was up 2 basis points to 4.932%. The 30-year Treasury bond yield — which often reacts the most to geopolitical developments — was down less than 1 basis point at 5.299%. "Assets that had offered a measure of safety last week have retreated today," said Thierry Wizman, global FX and rates strategist at Macquarie Group.

items.title: Indonesia searches for 34 missing workers after candy factory fire
items.body: JAKARTA (AP) -- Indonesian rescuers searched Monday for 34 missing workers after a deadly fire swept through a candy factory west of Jakarta. Saturday's fire broke out at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Banten province. Firefighters battled flames for about 14 hours before largely containing the blaze tearing through the three-story building. About 300 workers were inside the factory when the fire erupted, officials said. Of those, 63 were believed to have been in the hardest-hit area, mostly on the second floor where the flames originated from a cooling unit. Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency, or Basarnas, did not immediately offer a death toll, but said they collected human remains in 24 body bags for identification through forensic examination. Meanwhile, rescuers saved 29 workers, five of whom were hospitalized, and continue to search for the missing.

items.title: Grieving families getting into debt and doing without memorials due to benefit freezes
items.summary: MPs to discuss bereavement support as financial help for funeral expenses and bereaved families fails to keep pace with costs Bereaved families are borrowing money or forgoing a service with mourners because financial help available from the state no longer covers even half a…
items.body: Bereaved families are borrowing money or forgoing a service with mourners because financial help available from the state no longer covers even half a typical funeral director’s fee. “The funeral expenses payment (FEP) was originally meant to cover the cost of a simple funeral. Today, that is a pipe dream,” said Lindesay Mace, a co-manager of Down to Earth, a funeral costs support service run by the charity Quaker Social Action. For eligible households in England, Wales and Northern Ireland (Scotland has its own version), the benefit covers “reasonable” cemetery or crematorium fees plus up to £1,000 for “other funeral expenses”. While the first element of the payment has had to keep pace with inflation, the £1,000 cap has risen once in 23 years and has been frozen since 2020, despite rising fees for the elements of a funeral that it covers.

items.title: ‘Worst COP ever’: Climate talks collapse after draft deal fails to include fossil fuels
items.summary: Governments and campaigners rejected the "cover decision" drafted at the U.N.'s climate summit, COP31, on Sunday.
items.body: Negotiations at the United Nations' climate summit collapsed on Sunday as the U.K., EU and others rejected a draft deal that failed to include fossil fuels. Since the U.N.'s Climate Change Conference — or COP31 — began in Antalya, Turkey, on Nov. 9, almost 200 countries have been locked in talks to reach a "cover decision," with a number of drafts issued in recent days. Antonio Guterres, the U.N.'s secretary-general, said he was " deeply disappointed " that no consensus was reached. Talks centered on electrification, funding for developing nations and ways to respond to scientific warnings about rising global temperatures, with the 1.5 degrees Celsius target likely to be overshot. But on Sunday, after negotiations overran by almost two days, the latest cover proposal made no mention of fossil fuels, prompting outcry from governments and campaigners.

items.title: French biotech rejects short seller’s cancer-risk claims after shares plunge 17%
items.summary: Short seller Scorpion Capital has accused Abivax of serious scientific and safety shortcomings in its experimental inflammatory bowel disease drug.
items.body: French biotech Abivax 's stock has partially recovered after the company responded to short seller Scorpion Capital accusing it of serious scientific and safety shortcomings in its experimental inflammatory bowel disease drug, obefazimod. In a report published Friday, Scorpion alleged that Abivax's laboratory-commissioned tests indicated obefazimod may act through nonspecific toxic effects on cells, rather than the targeted biological mechanism the company described. Abivax's Paris-listed shares fell 17%. After the closing bell, Abivax said Scorpion's report contained "numerous factually inaccurate and misleading statements, assumptions, and conclusions." Obefazimod is Abivax's only drug. It has shown benefits for patients with ulcerative colitis in a late-stage trial. Abivax has said it aims to file for FDA approval by the end of the year, with a potential U.S. launch in 2027.

items.title: Househunter swaps Australia for Wales' most affordable town - where locals are struggling to buy
items.summary: The area has attracted investors and even a buyer from Australia, but locals struggle to afford homes.
items.body: A house-hunter has moved 10,000 miles (16,000km) from Australia to Wales' most affordable town because the properties are so cheap. James Brown, 56, spotted the three-bed house in Tylorstown, near Ferndale, Rhondda Cynon Taf, online for £80,000 and put an offer in. "It's ideal if you're commuting, and everything's virtually on your doorstep, so a really affordable area to come to," he said. But some people who live in Ferndale - dubbed Wales' most affordable town with an average property price of £116,200 - say they are still struggling to buy homes. Zoopla says a typical home in Ferndale costs "less than twice the annual wages of two full-time workers". The property selling website said its analysis shows this is the most affordable town in Wales.

items.title: Stuck: How a frozen housing market is hitting buyers, sellers and the economy
items.summary: A sharp spike in mortgage rates in September has pushed the already chilly real estate sector into a deep freeze.
items.body: Autumn is usually a busy time in the housing market, but not this year. A sharp spike in mortgage rates in September has pushed the already chilly real estate sector into a deep freeze . Buyers and sellers are moving to the sidelines, leaving those in the real estate business without much business. The average rate on the popular 30-year fixed mortgage hovered around 6.60% in July, according to Mortgage News Daily. By the start of October, it was at 7.61%, a full percentage point higher. "That shock, that rise of 100 basis points, is one of the fastest three-month increases we've seen in decades," said Zillow CEO Jeremy Wacksman on CNBC . While the jump in rates exacerbated the problem , the slowdown in the housing market has been building for years. Rising home prices have pushed the dream of homeownership out of reach for a growing number of Americans.

items.title: Yemen's Houthis claim attacks on Saudi oil refinery as Trump warns of new strikes next year
items.summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed an operation against Saudi Arabia's Rabigh oil refinery, as diplomatic efforts to end the war face long odds.
items.body: Yemen's Houthis, backed by Iran, said Sunday that they had targeted Rabigh oil refinery in Saudi Arabia, in the latest sign of worsening hostilities in the region, as Iranian forces seek to pressure the U.S. into accepting its terms. The Houthis said they has directly hit the infrastructure, though the extent of the damage remains unclear, Reuters reported. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said earlier in the day that it had "intercepted and destroyed" a drone launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia's western region, which included some of the country's critical energy refining and export infrastructure. Rabigh, about 165 kilometers north of Jeddah on the kingdom's western Red Sea coast, hosts Petro Rabigh, a major oil refining and petrochemical complex, developed by Saudi Aramco and Japan's Sumitomo Chemical.

items.title: US-India energy ties tighten as New Delhi snaps up Venezuelan oil
items.body: MUMBAI/NEW DELHI -- More than a year after U.S. President Donald Trump triggered a standoff with India over its purchases of Russian crude oil, Indian imports of Venezuelan crude and American liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) have surged, pointing to a tightening of energy ties between the two economies, even as Washington and New Delhi continue to negotiate a contentious, long-delayed trade deal.

items.title: 'Biggest U-turn in economic history': Experts react to Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
items.summary: The Nvidia CEO was reinstated after weeks of controversy over his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
items.body: Nvidia's board members have announced that they unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as the company's boss "effective immediately" - capping a remarkable U-turn in the technology firm's fortunes. The board had previously ruled out Huang's return after he admitted an affair with a woman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy. US President Donald Trump praised the decision, telling CNBC he made it happen, while Nvidia's share price shot up by more than 30% after a week of poor performance in the wake of the initial scandal. Experts from across the techonology and business sector reacted to his unexpected return.

items.title: Forget Anthropic: In Europe, the IPO hype is about a blue lagoon
items.summary: Iceland’s famed Blue Lagoon geothermal spa is going public in a $110 million IPO, tapping investor interest in tourism and the booming wellness industry.
items.body: While investors are fixated on Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut , a very different IPO is making waves in Europe: Iceland's Blue Lagoon, the operator of one of the world's most famous geothermal spas. Blue Lagoon Corp. raised roughly 14.3 billion Icelandic kronur ($110 million) through the offering, valuing the Icelandic geothermal spa operator at about $787 million, according to the company's investor presentation . The Blue Lagoon traces its origins to 1992, when Blue Lagoon Ltd. was founded to study the water in the Blue Lagoon, an open-air pool of warm, milky-blue water set in a black lava field in southwestern Iceland. It grew into a business spanning a spa, hotels and skincare made with ingredients from the lagoon.
